atus_work.assumptions: The designated diary day represents that person's days of its type; WT06's calibration population matches the target; BLS_WORK classifies activities as BLS does.
atus_work.estimand: Mean minutes per person-day of working and work-related activities (BLS major category; includes work-related travel), all 2023 person-days, U.S. civilian noninstitutional population aged 15 and older
atus_work.estimator: Weighted mean sum(w_i y_i) / sum(w_i) over all 2023 diaries, w = WT06
atus_work.explicit_weights: WT06, the ATUS final weight. Each diary counts for the number of person-days it represents: the 2023 weights sum to 99.0 billion person-days, about 365 for each of 271.3 million people. BLS constructs it so that weekday and weekend diaries add up to the weekday and weekend person-days in each quarter, for the population and selected subgroups.
atus_work.randomness: Sampling (ATUS draws households from those completing the CPS, one person aged 15+ per household, and assigns the diary day) and response.
atus_work.target_population: All 2023 person-days of the U.S. civilian noninstitutional population aged 15 and older
atus_work.title: How much do Americans work? All person-days (ATUS 2023)
atus_work.variance_estimator: Not computed. The store carries no ATUS replicate weights (BLS publishes them as RWT06), so an SE from WT06 alone would leave out the design, and its error could run in either direction.

atus_work_anywork.assumptions: The population is defined by the outcome, so this is a conditional mean (an intensive margin), not a population average.
atus_work_anywork.estimand: Mean minutes of working and work-related activities (BLS major category; includes work-related travel) on 2023 person-days that included any such activity, U.S. civilian noninstitutional population aged 15 and older
atus_work_anywork.estimator: Weighted mean over diaries with BLS_WORK above zero, w = WT06
atus_work_anywork.explicit_weights: WT06, the ATUS final weight. Each diary counts for the number of person-days it represents: the 2023 weights sum to 99.0 billion person-days, about 365 for each of 271.3 million people. BLS constructs it so that weekday and weekend diaries add up to the weekday and weekend person-days in each quarter, for the population and selected subgroups.
atus_work_anywork.implicit_weights: Relative to the all-days mean, days without work get zero weight.
atus_work_anywork.randomness: Sampling (ATUS draws households from those completing the CPS, one person aged 15+ per household, and assigns the diary day) and response.
atus_work_anywork.target_population: 2023 person-days with some work, U.S. civilian noninstitutional population aged 15 and older
atus_work_anywork.title: Days with any work (ATUS 2023)
atus_work_anywork.variance_estimator: Not computed. The store carries no ATUS replicate weights (BLS publishes them as RWT06), so an SE from WT06 alone would leave out the design, and its error could run in either direction.

atus_work_employed.assumptions: Employment status measured at the ATUS interview describes the diary day.
atus_work_employed.estimand: Mean minutes per person-day of working and work-related activities (BLS major category; includes work-related travel), 2023 person-days of people employed at their ATUS interview, U.S. civilian noninstitutional population aged 15 and older
atus_work_employed.estimator: Weighted mean over diaries with emp3 = Employed, w = WT06
atus_work_employed.explicit_weights: WT06, the ATUS final weight. Each diary counts for the number of person-days it represents: the 2023 weights sum to 99.0 billion person-days, about 365 for each of 271.3 million people. BLS constructs it so that weekday and weekend diaries add up to the weekday and weekend person-days in each quarter, for the population and selected subgroups.
atus_work_employed.implicit_weights: Relative to the all-days mean, person-days of people not employed get zero weight.
atus_work_employed.randomness: Sampling (ATUS draws households from those completing the CPS, one person aged 15+ per household, and assigns the diary day) and response.
atus_work_employed.target_population: 2023 person-days of employed members of the U.S. civilian noninstitutional population aged 15 and older
atus_work_employed.title: Employed people, all days (ATUS 2023)
atus_work_employed.variance_estimator: Not computed. The store carries no ATUS replicate weights (BLS publishes them as RWT06), so an SE from WT06 alone would leave out the design, and its error could run in either direction.

atus_work_employed_worked.assumptions: As above. BLS's headline 'hours worked on days worked' counts time working at jobs only, a narrower activity, so it is yet another estimand.
atus_work_employed_worked.estimand: Mean minutes of working and work-related activities (BLS major category; includes work-related travel) on 2023 person-days on which employed people did any such activity, U.S. civilian noninstitutional population aged 15 and older
atus_work_employed_worked.estimator: Weighted mean over diaries with emp3 = Employed and BLS_WORK above zero, w = WT06
atus_work_employed_worked.explicit_weights: WT06, the ATUS final weight. Each diary counts for the number of person-days it represents: the 2023 weights sum to 99.0 billion person-days, about 365 for each of 271.3 million people. BLS constructs it so that weekday and weekend diaries add up to the weekday and weekend person-days in each quarter, for the population and selected subgroups.
atus_work_employed_worked.implicit_weights: Relative to the all-days mean, zero weight on days of the non-employed and on non-work days.
atus_work_employed_worked.randomness: Sampling (ATUS draws households from those completing the CPS, one person aged 15+ per household, and assigns the diary day) and response.
atus_work_employed_worked.target_population: 2023 work days of employed members of the U.S. civilian noninstitutional population aged 15 and older
atus_work_employed_worked.title: Employed people, on days they worked (ATUS 2023)
atus_work_employed_worked.variance_estimator: Not computed. The store carries no ATUS replicate weights (BLS publishes them as RWT06), so an SE from WT06 alone would leave out the design, and its error could run in either direction.

atus_work_unweighted.assumptions: Only if the sample were a simple random sample of person-days would this target the population mean. ATUS is not one.
atus_work_unweighted.estimand: Mean minutes per person-day of working and work-related activities (BLS major category; includes work-related travel), all 2023 person-days, U.S. civilian noninstitutional population aged 15 and older
atus_work_unweighted.estimator: Unweighted mean of BLS_WORK over all 8,548 diaries
atus_work_unweighted.explicit_weights: None: every diary counts once. Weekend diaries are 48.9% of the sample but 28.8% of the weighted person-days, so they get far more than their share.
atus_work_unweighted.implicit_weights: Equal weights per diary, which over-represents weekend days and groups that respond more often.
atus_work_unweighted.randomness: Sampling (ATUS draws households from those completing the CPS, one person aged 15+ per household, and assigns the diary day) and response.
atus_work_unweighted.target_population: All 2023 person-days of the U.S. civilian noninstitutional population aged 15 and older (the same target as the weighted row)
atus_work_unweighted.title: All person-days, unweighted (ATUS 2023)
atus_work_unweighted.variance_estimator: Not computed. The store carries no ATUS replicate weights (BLS publishes them as RWT06), so an SE from WT06 alone would leave out the design, and its error could run in either direction.

atus_work_weekday.assumptions: As for all person-days. Holidays that fall on a weekday are included; BLS's own weekday tables exclude them.
atus_work_weekday.estimand: Mean minutes per person-day of working and work-related activities (BLS major category; includes work-related travel), Monday–Friday person-days in 2023, U.S. civilian noninstitutional population aged 15 and older
atus_work_weekday.estimator: Weighted mean over diaries with DAY in 2–6, w = WT06
atus_work_weekday.explicit_weights: WT06, the ATUS final weight. Each diary counts for the number of person-days it represents: the 2023 weights sum to 99.0 billion person-days, about 365 for each of 271.3 million people. BLS constructs it so that weekday and weekend diaries add up to the weekday and weekend person-days in each quarter, for the population and selected subgroups.
atus_work_weekday.implicit_weights: Relative to the all-days mean, weekend days get zero weight.
atus_work_weekday.randomness: Sampling (ATUS draws households from those completing the CPS, one person aged 15+ per household, and assigns the diary day) and response.
atus_work_weekday.target_population: Monday–Friday person-days in 2023 of the U.S. civilian noninstitutional population aged 15 and older
atus_work_weekday.title: Weekdays only (ATUS 2023)
atus_work_weekday.variance_estimator: Not computed. The store carries no ATUS replicate weights (BLS publishes them as RWT06), so an SE from WT06 alone would leave out the design, and its error could run in either direction.

foodsec_children.assumptions: A household's classification applies to every child in it. USDA's child-referenced measure, whether the children themselves were food insecure, is a different estimand.
foodsec_children.estimand: Share of children living in households classified food insecure over the previous 12 months
foodsec_children.estimator: sum(w_i y_h(i)) / sum(w_i) over children in households with a status, w = FSSUPPWT; y_h(i) is the status of child i's household
foodsec_children.explicit_weights: FSSUPPWT, the supplement person weight: each child counts for the children he or she represents.
foodsec_children.implicit_weights: Relative to the household rate, each household enters in proportion to the number of children in it; households without children drop out.
foodsec_children.randomness: Sampling of housing units, household response to the CPS, and response to the supplement.
foodsec_children.target_population: Children under 18 in the U.S. civilian noninstitutional population, December 2023
foodsec_children.title: Children in food-insecure households, 2023 (CPS December Food Security Supplement)
foodsec_children.variance_estimator: Not computed: the extract carries no replicate weights or design variables (weights-only tier).

foodsec_households.assumptions: The 18-item scale classifies households as USDA does; households with a missing status are ignorable.
foodsec_households.estimand: Share of households food insecure (low or very low food security over the previous 12 months, USDA definition)
foodsec_households.estimator: sum(w_h y_h) / sum(w_h) over householder records (PERNUM = 1) with a status, w = FSSUPPWTH
foodsec_households.explicit_weights: FSSUPPWTH, the supplement household weight: each household counts for the households it represents.
foodsec_households.implicit_weights: None beyond w; every household counts once regardless of its size.
foodsec_households.randomness: Sampling of housing units, household response to the CPS, and response to the supplement.
foodsec_households.target_population: U.S. households in the civilian noninstitutional population, December 2023
foodsec_households.title: Food insecurity among households, 2023 (CPS December Food Security Supplement)
foodsec_households.variance_estimator: Not computed: the extract carries no replicate weights or design variables (weights-only tier).

poverty_child_2021.assumptions: IPUMS POVERTY reproduces the official measure (IPUMS also offers OFFPOV, which this extract lacks); SPMPOV weighted by ASECWT reproduces Census SPM rates (the SPM weight is not in the extract); reported income and benefits are accurate enough for both measures.
poverty_child_2021.estimand: Two estimands: the share of children in families whose pre-tax money income is below the official threshold, and the share in SPM units whose resources after taxes, transfers, and necessary expenses are below the SPM threshold
poverty_child_2021.estimator: sum(w_i y_i) / sum(w_i) over children in each measure's universe, w = ASECWT
poverty_child_2021.implicit_weights: None beyond w. The universes differ slightly: the official measure excludes unrelated children under 15 (296 records in 2022); the SPM includes them.
poverty_child_2021.randomness: Sampling of housing units, household response, and ASEC supplement response.
poverty_child_2021.target_population: Children under 18 in the civilian noninstitutional population (ASEC universe), calendar year 2021
poverty_child_2021.title: Child poverty in 2021 under two definitions (CPS ASEC 2022)
poverty_child_2021.variance_estimator: Successive difference replication with the 160 person replicate weights: Var = (4/160) sum_r (theta_r - theta)^2, df = 159, centred on the full-sample estimate. svy 0.28 with method='replication' and variance_center='estimate', checked against a hand computation and R survey 4.5.

turnout_2020.assumptions: Supplement nonrespondents did not vote; respondents report their own voting accurately. Both are assumptions, not data.
turnout_2020.estimand: Share of that population who voted in the November 2020 election, as reported in the CPS
turnout_2020.estimator: Census convention: sum(w_i v_i) / sum(w_i) over every citizen adult with a positive supplement weight, where v_i = 1 for a reported vote and 0 otherwise, so supplement nonrespondents count as nonvoters. w = VOSUPPWT.
turnout_2020.explicit_weights: VOSUPPWT, identical on every record to WTFINL, the basic CPS final weight: base weight, household noninterview adjustment, and calibration to population controls. It carries no adjustment for supplement nonresponse.
turnout_2020.implicit_weights: None beyond w. The convention imputes 'did not vote' to the 15.7% (weighted) who did not answer; the respondents-only alternative instead gives them zero weight, which assumes they vote like respondents.
turnout_2020.randomness: Sampling of housing units, household response to the CPS, and person response to the supplement.
turnout_2020.target_population: U.S. citizens 18 and older in the civilian noninstitutional population, not in the armed forces, November 2020
turnout_2020.title: What was turnout? (CPS November 2020)
turnout_2020.variance_estimator: Not computed: the extract carries no replicate weights or design variables (weights-only tier); an SE from VOSUPPWT alone would not be design-based.
